summary: Glyph-part table of one message page: owns the array of 0xA8-byte message parts plus the owner object whose animation state the parts follow.
evidence: Ui_MessageParts_ApplyAnimCommand 0x003E1B58 walks parts = f_158 for partCount = f_15C entries of 0xA8 bytes and, for command 1, reads the owner's u16 animation state at f_160+0x4A (default 0x1B6); maybe_Ui_MessageParts_BuildGlyphParts 0x003E24A6 appends parts using the same f_158/f_15C pair and the 0x1C-byte page records.

fields.name: parts
fields.evidence: iVar1 = self->f_158; iVar3 = iVar1 + f_15C * 0xA8; the loops advance by 0xA8 per part and pass each part to Ui_Part_StoreAnimIndex / Ui_Part_UpdateAnimState

fields.name: partCount
fields.evidence: multiplier of the 0xA8 stride: end = parts + f_15C*0xA8, and BuildGlyphParts loops i < f_15C over the 0x1C-byte page entries

fields.name: owner
fields.evidence: null-checked before owner->f_4A (u16, read with ldrh) is used as the animation state handed to Ui_Part_UpdateAnimState; the owner is the message window that drives this part table

summary: Root of the message-window subsystem: a Ui_Object-derived object that owns an embedded state sequence at +0x3574 whose eight 0x18-byte state records drive the message windows.
evidence: Ctor 0x001959D8 stores the root vtable at +0, calls Ui_Object_InitMemberPair(self+0xD5D words = +0x3574), overrides the pair vtable with uRam00195ebc, writes the owner back-pointer to pair+0x20 and std_ConstructArray builds 8 x 0x18 state records at pair+0x24. The named std_StateSequence42_Tick/ChangeState/SetState treat pair+0x20 as their owner, so +0x3574 is an embedded std_StateSequence42. The batch size 13688 is only the last tracked offset; the embedded sequence extends the object to at least 0x3660.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: ctor writes the root vtable literal uRam00195eb8 to *puVar2 immediately after Ui_DiveForm_Ctor

fields.name: unknown_20
fields.evidence: Spurious batch field: `puVar3[8] = puVar2` writes the owner back-pointer at +0x20 of the embedded member pair (puVar3 = self+0x3574), not the root's own +0x20; no recovered function accesses the root at +0x20

fields.name: memberPair
fields.evidence: Ui_Object_InitMemberPair(self+0x3574), vtable override, owner back-link at pair+0x20 and eight 0x18-byte state records at pair+0x24; std_StateSequence42_Tick/ChangeState/SetState use pair+0x20 as their owner

summary: Slide-window event handler that enables exactly one of the three game-work mode flags 0x1A7..0x1A9 and shows/hides a child widget according to its mode byte.
evidence: maybe_Ui_ModePane_UpdateVisibility 0x004F0120 calls Ui_SlideWindow_OnEventB on entry (the base implementation), then branches on ldrb [r7,#0x2C8] (0/1/2 -> work flags 0x1A8/0x1A7/0x1A9) and finally calls slot +0x14 of the child pointer at +0x4C. The batch clusters one override of a slide window, so the class may be a fragment of Ui_SlideWindow (size 720); the name is kept as generated.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: No direct store in this method, but it overrides the base Ui_SlideWindow_OnEventB called at entry, so +0 is the polymorphic vtable pointer; the batch's '+0 read' is really the child vtable loaded from +0x4C

fields.name: visibilityTarget
fields.evidence: asm `ldr r0,[r7,#0x4c]; ldr r2,[r0,#0x14]; blx r2` at 0x004F0328 calls virtual slot +0x14 on this child widget with the computed visible flag

fields.name: mode
fields.evidence: asm `ldrb r0,[r7,#0x2c8]`; values 0, 1, 2 select work flags 0x1A8, 0x1A7, 0x1A9 and any other value returns early. Batch width 4 is a pointer-arithmetic artefact; the store/load is a single byte

summary: Multiple-inheritance UI object: primary vtable at +0, a secondary interface vtable at +0x258 and an embedded Ui_Object base at +0x278; its deleting destructor unlinks and frees the whole object.
evidence: Deleting dtor 0x004F057C: asm `str r1,[r0],#0x258` installs the primary vtable and advances to +0x258, `str r2,[r0],#0x20` installs the secondary table there, then Ui_Object_DtorBody(self+0x278) and Field_SceneObject_Dtor(self+0x278-0x278) destroy and free the object; the entry is vtable slot 0x77C2C8.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: `*param_1 = param_2;` stores the primary vtable supplied by the deleting destructor

fields.name: secondaryVtable
fields.evidence: `self[0x96] = vtable + 0xD4` (word 0x96 = byte +0x258) installs the secondary interface table of the multiple-inheritance object

fields.name: objectBase
fields.evidence: Ui_Object_DtorBody(self+0x278) destroys the embedded Ui_Object base sub-object; the dtor then calls Field_SceneObject_Dtor on the same address

summary: Small number/text pane: binds the 'num' pane at Init, keeps the pane-set id at +0x28 and writes item/quantity text through the text element based at +0xD4.
evidence: Ui_NumberPane_Init 0x004F247C: drN base ctor, then virtual +0x34(self, 'num' @0x4F24BC, (u16)f_28 << 16, 0); asm `ldrh r1,[r4,#0x28]`. maybe_Ui_NumberPane_SetIconAndText uses the same f_28. maybe_Ui_NumberPane_Show 0x002C2DC4 does `add r5,r5,#0xD4` and passes that address to Ui_TextElement_SetString. The batch groups three methods that may belong to different widgets, so only the offsets are named.

fields.name: paneSetId
fields.evidence: asm `ldrh r1,[r4,#0x28]` in Init; passed as the high 16 bits of the pane id to the named-pane binder for the 'num' pane, and shifted the same way in SetIconAndText

fields.name: unknown_vtableSlot34
fields.evidence: Artifact: the quoted line is the virtual call (**(code **)(*self + 0x34))(self,'num',...), i.e. vtable slot 0x34, and 0x34*4 = 0xD0. Init asm touches only [r4] and [r4,#0x28]; no +0xD0 data access exists

fields.name: maybe_textElementBase
fields.evidence: Show adds 0xD4 to self (`add r5,r5,#0xD4` at 0x002C2DF4) and passes the result as the first argument of Ui_TextElement_SetString; +0xD4 is therefore the start of an embedded text-element/window sub-object whose extent is beyond the batch size 216

summary: Animation-frame helper on a layout node (probably a fragment of Ui_Layout): applies a frame to the anim node at +0x11C, then recurses into the animatable children of the child list at +0x140 while +0x138 is non-zero.
evidence: maybe_Ui_PaneAnim_ApplyToChildren 0x0038295C: Ui_Widget_UpdateAnimatedChildren(); Ui_Layout_ApplyAnimFrame(&self->f_11C, target, frame, flags); then if (f_138 != 0 && f_140 != 0) it walks the intrusive list at f_140->f_10 and forwards every child whose class RTTI is not 0x007AE8A0. Ui_Layout_ApplyAnimFrame's first parameter is a UiAnimNode*.

fields.name: animNode
fields.evidence: &self->f_11C is passed as the UiAnimNode* to Ui_Layout_ApplyAnimFrame, which reads node+4 and node->f_C

fields.name: maybe_hasAnimChildren
fields.evidence: Only use is the first half of the gate `if (f_138 != 0 && f_140 != 0)` before the child-list walk; no writer and no other reader, so the flag's meaning beyond 'non-zero enables the walk' is unproven

fields.name: childListOwner
fields.evidence: f_140->f_10 is the head of an intrusive child list (piVar6 = iVar2->f_10; piVar6 != &iVar2->f_10; piVar6 = *piVar6); entry[2] is a child widget whose class is checked against 0x007AE8A0

summary: Integer screen-space rectangle (x, y, width, height) used by the UI element overlap test.
evidence: Ui_Rect_IntersectsElement 0x00668774 treats the argument as int[4]: `rect[0] < b.x+b.w && rect[1] < b.y+b.h && b.x < rect[0]+rect[2] && b.y < rect[1]+rect[3]`, where b is the element's bounds callback output.

fields.name: y
fields.evidence: rect[1] is the vertical origin in both comparisons (rect[1] < b.y+b.h and b.y < rect[1]+rect[3])

fields.name: width
fields.evidence: rect[2] is added to rect[0] to form the right edge tested against the element's left edge

fields.name: height
fields.evidence: rect[3] is added to rect[1] to form the bottom edge tested against the element's top edge

summary: Animation span: an array of 0xC-byte animation key entries plus an optional timeline id; Ui_Span_IsIdle reports when the timeline and every keyed object have finished.
